--- title: "Outbreak Detectives: Can You Stop the Spread?" author: "R-Ladies+ Melbourne" output: html_document: toc: true toc_float: true theme: readable --- # Emergency Alert Several local hospitals have reported an unusual increase in sick students from the same school. Students from two classrooms have presented with a range of symptoms, and the number of cases is continuing to grow. Your team has joined the **Global Outbreak Investigation Unit**. Your job is to work out what is happening. Do not diagnose the outbreak yet. Follow the evidence. Possible causes include: - Influenza A - COVID-19 - Zombie Virus A - Malaria - RSV (Respiratory syncytial virus) - Rhinovirus - Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) - Toxoplasmosis Your job is to follow the evidence. --- # 1. Hospital records have arrived First, open the patient file. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} patients_raw <- load_patients() ``` ::: Take a look. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} head(patients_raw) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
patient_id first_name class age sex temperature_c hours_to_symptoms hospitalised case_status fever cough sore_throat headache muscle_aches vomiting diarrhoea loss_of_smell bleeding confusion
P01 Alex 9A 16 female 37.3 72.0 YES SICK yes Y No YES yes N No NO no N
P02 Amelia 9A 13 F 37.8 121.0 yes sick Y Yes NO yes N No NO no N No
P03 Ari 9A 15 male 37.5 191.3 N yes No YES yes Y Yes YES no N No NO
P04 Bailey 9A 13 Female 38.3 109.7 No Sick YES yes Y Yes YES no N No NO no
P05 Charlie 9A 14 male 37.7 124.9 YES SICK yes Y Yes NO no N No NO no N
P06 Chloe 9A 13 Male 37.4 180.7 yes sick Y Yes NO no N No NO no N No
````` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} names(patients_raw) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "patient_id" "first_name" "class" [4] "age" "sex" "temperature_c" [7] "hours_to_symptoms" "hospitalised" "case_status" [10] "fever" "cough" "sore_throat" [13] "headache" "muscle_aches" "vomiting" [16] "diarrhoea" "loss_of_smell" "bleeding" [19] "confusion" ``` ::: ::: ### What do you notice? - What does one row represent? - What information do we have about each student? - Can you spot anything messy? --- # 2. Clean the data The hospital entered the records very quickly. For example: `Yes`, `YES`, `yes` and `Y` all mean the same thing. Instead of fixing every value ourselves, we can use a function. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} patients <- clean_data(patients_raw) ``` ::: Did it work? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} count_cases(patients) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
case_status students
Sick 71
Well 24
````` ::: ::: ### Why clean data? Computers need us to be consistent. If `"Yes"` and `"YES"` are written differently, R may think they are different answers. --- # 3. How many students are sick? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} count_cases(patients) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
case_status students
Sick 71
Well 24
````` ::: ::: Now look at the students with the highest temperatures. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} show_sickest(patients) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
patient_id first_name temperature_c hospitalised
P08 Dev 38.4 Yes
P16 Isaac 38.4 Yes
P31 Sam 38.4 Yes
P04 Bailey 38.3 No
P13 Harper 38.3 Yes
P23 Maya 38.3 No
````` ::: ::: ### Your turn What do you notice about their temperatures? --- # 4. What symptoms are most common? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} symptom_table(patients) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
symptom n
cough 48
sore_throat 36
fever 34
muscle_aches 27
headache 21
diarrhoea 18
vomiting 14
loss_of_smell 3
````` ::: ::: Now make a graph. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} symptoms <- symptom_table(patients) ggplot(symptoms, aes( x = n, y = reorder(symptom, n) )) + geom_col(fill = "purple") + labs( title = "Symptoms reported by sick students", x = "Number of students", y = "Symptom" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Outbreak_Detectives_files/figure-revealjs/symptom-plot-1.png){width=864} ::: ::: ### Try editing the graph Change `"purple"` to another colour and run the code again. You can also change the words inside `title =`, `x =` and `y =`. ### Think like a disease detective Which symptoms stand out? Does this help rule out any diseases? --- # 5. Do sick students have higher temperatures? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(patients, aes( x = case_status, y = temperature_c, fill = case_status )) + geom_boxplot() + labs( title = "Do sick students have higher temperatures?", x = "Student group", y = "Temperature (°C)" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Outbreak_Detectives_files/figure-revealjs/temperature-1.png){width=864} ::: ::: ### Try editing the graph Inside `aes()`, change: ```r fill = case_status ``` to: ```r colour = case_status ``` What changes? ### What do you notice? Compare the middle of the two boxplots. --- # 6. How quickly did students become sick? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} show_onset(patients) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
sick_students typical_temperature typical_hours_to_symptoms
71 37.7 116
````` ::: ::: The time between being exposed and becoming sick can be an important clue. --- # 7. New evidence: locations A second file has arrived. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} locations <- load_locations() ``` ::: We need information from **both files**. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} investigation <- combine_evidence( patients, locations ) ``` ::: Now find the locations with the most illness. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} location_table(investigation) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
location students sick attack_rate
Before-school swimming practice 15 15 1.0000000
Lunch area 15 15 1.0000000
Art class 10 10 1.0000000
International airport / return flight 1 1 1.0000000
Classroom 9A 31 19 0.6129032
Hockey training 20 11 0.5500000
Classroom 9B 12 0 0.0000000
Lunch courtyard 24 0 0.0000000
Swimming practice - did not enter pool 15 0 0.0000000
````` ::: ::: And plot them. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} locations_summary <- location_table(investigation) ggplot(locations_summary, aes( x = attack_rate, y = reorder(location, attack_rate) )) + geom_col(fill = "skyblue") + labs( title = "Where were sick students exposed?", x = "Attack rate", y = "Location" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Outbreak_Detectives_files/figure-revealjs/location-plot-1.png){width=864} ::: ::: ### Try editing the graph Change `"skyblue"` to `"orange"`, `"green"` or another colour. Then try changing the graph title. ### What does this tell us? Does one location or activity stand out? Could there be more than one explanation? --- # 8. Make a preliminary diagnosis Open the disease clue sheet. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} disease_clues <- load_disease_clues() disease_clues ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
disease fever cough vomiting diarrhoea confusion_or_bleeding typical_onset common_exposure
RSV (Respiratory syncytial virus) Low / possible Very common Uncommon Rare Rare 2–8 days Close respiratory contact; classrooms, lunch, activities
Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) Possible Common Possible Rare Rare 3–6 days Respiratory spread
Influenza A High Common Sometimes Uncommon Rare 1–4 days Respiratory spread
COVID-19 Possible Common Sometimes Possible Rare 2–5 days Respiratory spread
Rhinovirus Usually low Common Rare Rare Rare 1–3 days Respiratory spread
Cryptosporidiosis Possible Rare Common Very common Rare 1–12 days; average ~7 Contaminated swimming pool water
Toxoplasmosis Possible Rare Rare Rare Rare Variable Food, soil or cat faeces
Eimeriosis Variable Rare Possible Possible Rare Variable Primarily animal-associated parasite
Malaria (Plasmodium spp.) Common Rare Possible Possible Possible Usually 7+ days Mosquito exposure
````` ::: ::: Before you see the laboratory results, decide: 1. What disease do you think is spreading? 2. What evidence supports your answer? 3. Is there anything unusual about two of the sick students? --- # 9. Breaking News: sequencing results Patient records have arrived from several hospitals. The records were assembled quickly by different staff members, so some values may be written inconsistently. Most of the students who became sick have visited hospital at some stage during the investigation. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} show_tree( sample_colour = "red", reference_colour = "grey30", title = "Which reference is closest to the outbreak samples?" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Outbreak_Detectives_files/figure-revealjs/tree-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ### Read the tree - Which reference is closest to most of the student samples? - Do all of the student samples belong to the same group? - What do you notice about P29 and P30? A tree can tell us which samples are genetically similar. It **cannot** prove exactly who infected whom. --- # 10. Contact tracing Interviewers have now told us who spent time together. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} contacts <- load_contacts() ``` ::: How many separate groups are in the contact data? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} network_groups(contacts) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 80 ``` ::: ::: Now draw the network. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} network <- show_network( contacts, patients, sick_colour = "red", well_colour = "blue", title = "Who had contact with whom?" ) network ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Outbreak_Detectives_files/figure-revealjs/network-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ### Investigate the network - Are most sick students connected? - What is unusual about P29 and P30? - Why might some connected students still be well? - Does a connection prove that infection occurred? --- # 11. Final diagnosis Your team must now give the outbreak response team its answer. ### Main outbreak What is the most likely disease? ### Give three pieces of evidence You could use: - symptoms - time to illness - locations - sequencing - contact network --- # The bigger lesson Real outbreak investigations combine different types of evidence. No single graph gives us the whole answer. Today you used: **data + coding + epidemiology + genomics + networks** to solve an outbreak.

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
